commands.author: clawsweeper[bot]
commands.review_summary:
The branch changes Codex dynamic-tool timeout resolution so per-call timeoutSeconds is honored with a 30s outer watchdog grace when timeoutMs is absent, and side-question dynamic tool calls reuse the shared handler and resolver.

PR surface: Source -113, Tests +57. Total -56 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main ignores call.arguments.timeoutSeconds in the dynamic-tool timeout reader while sessions_send exposes timeoutSeconds as an integer tool argument. I did not run a live Codex app-server timeout turn in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow docs repair remains: the public Codex harness timeout docs still omit the new per-call timeoutSeconds fallback and 30s headroom behavior.

target.title: fix(codex): honor timeoutSeconds for dynamic tool calls when timeoutMs is absent
target.body:
Fixes #98864.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex dynamic tool calls can specify `timeoutSeconds` while omitting `timeoutMs`. `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` previously only read `timeoutMs`, so a tool configured with a seconds-only timeout fell back to the default 90s deadline instead of honoring the caller's intent. The side-question path (`resolveSideDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs`) had the same gap. Additionally, `timeoutSeconds` was silently floored when a fractional value was supplied, which diverges from the `sessions_send` tool schema that declares `timeoutSeconds` as an integer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` now falls back to `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs(value.timeoutSeconds)` when `timeoutMs` is absent or invalid.
- `readSideDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` mirrors the main path and also falls back to `readSideTimeoutSecondsAsMs(value.timeoutSeconds)`.
- Both `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` and `readSideTimeoutSecondsAsMs` now require `Number.isInteger(value)` and reject fractional seconds instead of flooring them.
- `timeoutMs` still takes precedence when both are present.

## User Impact

Dynamic tools that pass `timeoutSeconds` (e.g. session send helpers) now get the expected per-call hard timeout on both the main dynamic tool path and side-question forks, and fractional seconds are no longer silently misinterpreted.

## Evidence

Unit tests:

```bash
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  60 passed (60)
```

Real behavior proof (exercises the actual runtime handlers with a tool that intentionally sleeps past the deadline):

```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/codex-dynamic-tool-timeout-seconds.mts
```

```
=== Proof: Codex dynamic tool timeoutSeconds support ===

resolver/main: timeoutSeconds only: expected 30000ms, got 30000ms PASS
resolver/main: timeoutMs takes precedence: expected 5000ms, got 5000ms PASS
resolver/main: non-positive timeoutSeconds falls back to default: expected 90000ms, got 90000ms PASS
resolver/main: fractional timeoutSeconds falls back to default: expected 90000ms, got 90000ms PASS
resolver/side: timeoutSeconds only: expected 45000ms, got 45000ms PASS
resolver/side: timeoutMs takes precedence: expected 5000ms, got 5000ms PASS
resolver/side: fractional timeoutSeconds falls back to default: expected 90000ms, got 90000ms PASS
runtime/main: timeoutSeconds is enforced by handleDynamicToolCallWithTimeout: PASS
runtime/main: timeoutMs still takes precedence over timeoutSeconds: PASS
runtime/side: timeoutSeconds is enforced by handleSideDynamicToolCallWithTimeout: PASS
runtime/side: timeoutMs still takes precedence over timeoutSeconds: PASS

All cases passed.
```
